conventions.convention: Functionals take values in (−∞,+∞]; properness is relative to the admissible set and means existence of a finite competitor. Weak lower semicontinuity is sequential. Coercivity means bounded finite sublevels.
Convexity uses real coefficients; 0·(+∞)=0 is stipulated only for convex combinations. Strict inequalities are required for distinct finite competitors and weights strictly between zero and one.
Gâteaux differentiability requires all directional limits to constitute a bounded linear functional; existence of directional limits alone does not suffice.

The abstract direct method assumes the ultrafilter lemma, DC and HB. Trace-based applications explicitly assume AC. The weaker Sobolev completeness uses cite the supplier's actual CC-only proof, which was opened.
Fixed-trace variations lie in W₀¹ᵖ. The Euler–Lagrange sign is −div(fξ)+fs=0; free variations additionally give fξ·ν=0 with the outward normal.

Obstacle functions and competitors are real Sobolev classes. In dimension one the domain is a bounded interval and trace order is componentwise; in higher dimensions it is a bounded C¹ domain and boundary order is almost everywhere. Tψ≤0 is equivalent to ψ⁺∈H₀¹.

The reaction pairs bilinearly with tests. A pointwise complementarity product is asserted with an L² reaction density and continuous representatives; the measure version separately assumes a nonnegative Radon representation and continuous representatives.

Means and variances are divided by the squared L² norm, require a nonzero function and finite second moments, and use the negative-sign 2π Fourier convention. The general transform here is the Plancherel class.

Hardy assumes n≥1, positive a,b,C, a spatial Gaussian bound almost everywhere and a frequency bound everywhere for the continuous L¹ transform. Critical classification is almost everywhere, with scalar f̂(0)a^(n/2).
Finite supports are nonzero sets in Z/NZ, with N≥1, counting norms and the negative-sign N^(−1/2)-normalised DFT. The support product bound is N, including equality at N=1.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma, DC and HB. Let X be a real reflexive Banach space, A⊆X nonempty and weakly sequentially closed, and I:A→(−∞,+∞] proper, coercive on A and weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous on A. Then I attains its infimum on A. A may be convex and norm closed.

Assume HB and Countable Choice. Let X be a real normed space, K⊆X nonempty and convex, and I:K→(−∞,+∞] convex and sequentially lower semicontinuous in the norm topology. Then I is weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous on K.

Let X be a real Banach space, U⊆X open and F:U→R Gâteaux differentiable at a local minimiser u∈U. Then δF(u;v)=0 for every v∈X. More generally, local minimality on (u+V)∩U for a linear subspace V gives vanishing for every v∈V.
Assume the ultrafilter lemma, DC and HB. Let Ω⊆Rⁿ be open, n≥1, and 1<p<∞. Then the real Banach space W¹ᵖ(Ω) is reflexive.

Assume AC. Let X be a real Banach space, U⊆X open, I:U→R Fréchet differentiable at u, and G=(G₁,…,Gₘ):U→Rᵐ C¹ with DG(u) surjective. If u is a local minimum or maximum on {G=G(u)}, there is a unique λ∈Rᵐ with DI(u)=ΣᵢλᵢDGᵢ(u).

Assume Countable Choice. Let H be a real Hilbert space, K⊆H nonempty, closed and convex, a:H×H→R a bounded coercive bilinear form with constants M,α>0, without assuming symmetry, and F a bounded linear functional. There is exactly one u∈K with a(u,v−u)≥F(v−u) for every v∈K.

Assume AC. On a bounded interval I=(a,b), for real W¹ᵖ classes with 1≤p<∞, endpoint trace T is well defined, linear and bounded, with ker T=W₀¹ᵖ(I). For every real k, (u−k)⁺∈W¹ᵖ, T((u−k)⁺)=(Tu−k)⁺, and (u−k)⁺∈W₀¹ᵖ iff Tu≤(k,k). Also T(u⁺)=(Tu)⁺, T(u⁻)=(Tu)⁻ and T|u|=|Tu|.
Assume AC. Let Ω⊆Rⁿ be bounded open, n≥1, and (uⱼ)⊆H₀¹(Ω) norm bounded with uⱼ⇀u weakly in H₀¹ and ‖uⱼ‖₂=1 for every j. Then u∈H₀¹, ‖u‖₂=1, and some subsequence converges to u in L².
Assume Countable Choice. Let n≥1, j∈{1,…,n}, f∈H¹(Rⁿ;C) and xf∈L²(Rⁿ;Cⁿ), with H¹=W¹² under the regular-distribution identification. Then ‖xⱼf‖₂‖Dⱼf‖₂≥½‖f‖₂².
Let a,b>0 and F:C→C entire. If C₁,C₂≥0 satisfy |F(x+iy)|≤C₁exp(πy²/a) and |F(x)|≤C₂exp(−πbx²) for all real x,y, then F≡0 when ab>1; when ab=1, F(z)=F(0)exp(−πz²/a) for every complex z.

Assume Countable Choice. Let n≥1, a>0, C≥0 and measurable f satisfy |f(x)|≤Cexp(−πa|x|²) almost everywhere. Its Fourier–Laplace integral converges absolutely and is representative-independent at every z∈Cⁿ, has entire coordinate slices with derivative ∫f(x)(−2πixⱼ)exp(−2πix·z)dx, equals f̂ at every real point, and satisfies |F(z)|≤Ca^(−n/2)exp(π|Im z|²/a).
Let N≥1 and nonzero f∈C^(Z/NZ), with the unitary DFT. Then |supp f|·|supp F_Nf|≥N. At N=1 equality holds for every nonzero f.

concerns.concern: F1 restates thm-direct-method-in-a-reflexive-banach-space with a proper ambient I:X→(−∞,+∞], whereas the supplier requires I:A→(−∞,+∞] proper on A. Proof 1.1 consequently says all supplier hypotheses are met without establishing a finite competitor in A. The owned existence claim is nevertheless true: if I|A≡+∞ every point of nonempty A attains the infimum; otherwise I|A is proper and the supplier applies. The source citation and this missing split need adjudication; the same mismatch is already recorded in the current batch-15 frontier-ledger entry.

F5 says 'for φ∈C_c∞(−1,1) the pairing against the density 1_[−t,t] is ∫_{ {−t,t} }1_[−t,t]φ dx=0'. The whole reaction pairing is ∫_[−t,t]φ dx and is generally nonzero, as Verification 2.1 correctly proves. F5 needs to describe the contribution restricted to the two endpoints, rather than call it the pairing against the density.

seams_checked.note: cor-minimisers-are-classical-when-elliptic-regularity-applies case (ii) retains the supplier's n≥2, AC/CC, bounded C²,α domain, f∈C⁰,α and g∈C²,α hypotheses and its classical boundary conclusion.

Smooth regularity is applied to v=u₀−G with zero trace and smoothly extended forcing f+ΔG, then the lift is restored. The nonzero-trace Poisson argument uses the lifting supplier's fixed-R estimate and proves classical-to-weak consistency directly, without inflating the zero-trace classical supplier.

The higher-dimensional obstacle definition uses exactly the positive-part trace equivalence under AC/CC and bounded C¹ regularity. Lewy–Stampacchia uses admissible Sobolev truncations with a continuous H⁻¹ reaction and separately assumes Lψ∈L²; it does not claim arbitrary L¹ sources pair with all H₀¹ tests.

The support-product proof uses counting Parseval and the negative-sign N^(−1/2) DFT without attributing invertibility to its definition. The constant-function computation uses character-orthogonality parameters 0,k. All uses include N=1 correctly.
